note: 2022 MCM B, team 2200084. 18 figure rows (15 numbered in the report body plus the unnumbered poster photograph and the two restarted-number leaflet figures) and 3 printed tables, over 25 measured regions with 4 exclusions, unaccounted = 0. Shapes that need reading before the fields make sense: Figure 2 is the whole paper as one 2x2+1 poster diagram with miniature copies of two other figures inside it; Figure 3 is a basin map with two circular satellite insets cut into it; Figures 7 and 8 are two concentric doughnut rings, not pies, recorded as family 'other' because the vocabulary has no part-to-whole member; Figure 12 is grouped bars read off a blue left axis with three rate lines read off a green right axis; and Figures 9 and 10 are Sankey flows whose right-hand node column runs past the measured region, so their node lists are lower bounds. Nothing here is three-dimensional. Four regions are excluded as not-an-exhibit and all four are algorithm listings (Algorithm 1 on p9, Algorithm 2's title band and body on p16, Algorithm 3 on p16): they are typeset pseudo-code in a box, not artwork. The two-page poster at the back restarts the figure numbering at 1 and reprints existing artwork - p23's Figure 2 is Figure 5 in miniature and p24's Figure 3 is an enlarged Figure 11 - while p23's Figure 1 (a stacked area of drought-class shares over 2005-2020) is the leaflet's only new drawing. Printing errors kept verbatim: Table 3 reuses Table 2's caption ('List of Water Level Constraints') over an auction allotment grid, Figures 7 and 8 print their two captions in two columns so they interleave line by line, Figure 6's legend spells 'Ganyon' and prints the same '(lowest)' entry twice, and the cross-reference style 'figure [3]' / 'tab [2]' / 'figure[4.2]' / 'figre [4.2]' collides with the bibliography numbering [1]-[10]. The chapter-6 heading is indexed with its own word break ('Independent Pri-') and is recorded that way. doc_order is the measured geometry's own top-to-bottom order, so the two side-by-side pairs put the taller column first: Figure 8 (top 547.4 pt) precedes Figure 7 (548.5) on p11 and Figure 10 (129.4) precedes Figure 9 (136.6) on p12, although the printed caption order is 7 before 8 and 9 before 10.
rules: The paper splits its exhibits by chapter and the split is clean: chapter 1 carries the two context pictures, chapter 3 carries the notation table, chapter 4 carries the whole model apparatus and its first results, chapter 6 carries the auction exhibits, chapter 7 carries the two sensitivity charts, and every one of those is a single-framed exhibit [place.section_path] [place.section_kind] [geometry.family].

Part-to-whole is always drawn as two concentric doughnut rings with leader-line percentages, never as a bar, and there is no pie or doughnut family in the vocabulary, so Figures 7 and 8 are recorded as family 'other' [geometry.family] [geometry.printed_numbers].

Nothing in the paper is three-dimensional and nothing is a surface: three_d is 'no' and colorbar is false on all 21 rows, and the two depth-looking drawings - the dam series configuration and the IPV causal loop - are flat schematic boxes [geometry.three_d] [geometry.colorbar].

Table shape follows the data shape and units decide the header: the glossary goes tall and thin (6x2) because rows are symbols, the water-level grid goes wide (2x5) with the unit pasted into every cell because values are readings, and the auction grid goes wide and numeric (7x6) because rows are auction conditions and columns are states [table.rows] [table.cols] [table.units_in_header].

Rule style is booktabs everywhere with no zebra striping anywhere; the two result grids add exactly one vertical rule, between the stub column and the numbers, which is why those two rows read 'vertical-rules' and the glossary reads 'booktabs' [table.rule_style] [table.zebra].

Captions are noun phrases printed under a fixed frame - 'Figure N: <noun phrase>' or 'Table N: <noun phrase>' - with no verb, no unit and no conclusion, and the caption position is 'below' on all 20 numbered rows [caption.verbatim] [caption.voice] [caption.position].

Prose finds the exhibits through bracketed numbers inside a running sentence - 'as you can see below figure [3]', '(figure [5])', '(figure[11])', 'in figure[7] and figure[8]', 'in figure[4.2]', 'in tab [3]' - never through 'Figure N shows', and the bracket form is reused for citations, so a reader cannot tell a cross-reference from a reference number [mention.lead_sentence] [mention.lead_pattern].
